name: Question 12
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128542/assets/19f21fa7abb989e8c2bf35552675f498969e30e1f42012fd615c00686d20cb01.png)

Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 3,\,\,\frac{3\pi }{5}\le v\le \frac{6\pi }{7}\},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Find the image of $Δ$ under the action of $T.$
worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we transform each side of $Δ$ separately:

- Consider the image of the bottom side, where we have $v=\frac{3\pi }{5}$ and $1\le u\le 3.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{3\pi }{5}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{5}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{5})).\end{aligned}
$$

This line segment makes an angle of $\frac{3\pi }{5}$ with the positive $x$-axis in the $xy$-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii $1$ and $3$ centered at $O.$

- Consider the image of the top side, where we have $v=\frac{6\pi }{7}$ and $1\le u\le 3.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{6\pi }{7}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{6\pi }{7}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{6\pi }{7})).\end{aligned}
$$

This line segment makes an angle of $\frac{6\pi }{7}$ with the positive $x$-axis in the $xy$-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii $1$ and $3$ centered at $O.$

- Consider the image of the left side, where we have $u=1$ and $\frac{3\pi }{5}\le v\le \frac{6\pi }{7}.$ 

Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v).\end{aligned}
$$

This is an arc of the circle of radius $1$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{5}$ and $\theta =\frac{6\pi }{7}.$

- Consider the image of the right side, where we have $u=3$ and $\frac{3\pi }{5}\le v\le \frac{6\pi }{7}.$ 

Substituting $u=3$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(3\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡v).\end{aligned}
$$

This is an arc of the circle of radius $3$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{5}$ and $\theta =\frac{6\pi }{7}.$

Therefore, the image $D$ of $Δ$ under the action of $T$ is the region that is enclosed between 

- two circles with polar equations $r=1$ and $r=3,$ and

- two rays with polar equations $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{5}$ and $\theta =\frac{6\pi }{7},$

as shown in the diagram below.

EXPLANATION

To map the entire region Δ onto the xy-plane, we transform each side of Δ separately:

  • Consider the image of the bottom side, where we have v=3π5 and 1≤u≤3.

    Substituting v=3π5 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(ucos⁡(3π5),usin⁡(3π5)). This line segment makes an angle of 3π5 with the positive x-axis in the xy-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii 1 and 3 centered at O.

  • Consider the image of the top side, where we have v=6π7 and 1≤u≤3.

    Substituting v=6π7 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(ucos⁡(6π7),usin⁡(6π7)). This line segment makes an angle of 6π7 with the positive x-axis in the xy-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii 1 and 3 centered at O.

  • Consider the image of the left side, where we have u=1 and 3π5≤v≤6π7.

    Substituting u=1 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(cos⁡v,sin⁡v). This is an arc of the circle of radius 1 centered at the origin in the xy-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays θ=3π5 and θ=6π7.

  • Consider the image of the right side, where we have u=3 and 3π5≤v≤6π7.

    Substituting u=3 into our transformation equations, we obtain (x,y)=(3cos⁡v,3sin⁡v). This is an arc of the circle of radius 3 centered at the origin in the xy-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays θ=3π5 and θ=6π7.

Therefore, the image D of Δ under the action of T is the region that is enclosed between

  • two circles with polar equations r=1 and r=3, and

  • two rays with polar equations θ=3π5 and θ=6π7,

as shown in the diagram below.
